brief.situation: You configure the HR assistant at Tallis & Rowe Engineering (fictional). It uses a Gemini model on Google Cloud with grounding turned on so it would 'stop making things up'. In the pilot it answered leave questions with figures from other companies' websites. It launches to all 1,400 staff at 10:00. It is 09:05.
handover: The HR handbook and policy PDFs are indexed in an Agent Search data store, hr-policies, built last week.
The pilot's grounding setting was copied from a marketing demo.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

scoring.modelReasoning: The answers cite public websites, so the grounding source is the problem: Google Search grounding connects the model to world data, while the leave policy lives in the company's handbook. Ground on the hr-policies data store and check the test questions cite it. An instruction to use company policy cannot supply the policy; a lower temperature changes sampling, not where facts come from.
